audit.why: Win rate 52.63% over 3409 games matches the data.

audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart carries a blanket 'Skill' on all seven rows while the content layer and packet chart both give Viktor levels 1-6, Skill at first item, Veigar at 2+ items. Two layers render different answers.
audit.why: Viktor's Siphon Power shield + empowered auto and Hextech Ray waveclear win early; Veigar's uncapped stacking wins late. Content layer and packet agree; full layer is the stale one.
audit.corrected: Full phases[0-4].side -> Viktor, phases[6].side -> Veigar, whys rewritten to match; content win[] already correct.

audit.why: Spikes are right in shape (Viktor 3-5, even 6/first item, Veigar 2+ items) but two spike texts carried wrong ability names — fixed under point 4.

audit.whatIsWrong: Fabricated/renamed abilities: 'Death Ray' (really Hextech Ray, E), 'Chaos Storm' (really Arcane Storm, R), and spikes[0] labels Gravity Field as E when it is W. Missing interaction: Arcane Storm is a channel and Event Horizon's stun cancels it outright. breakdown.cooldowns had no numbers.
audit.why: Kit file is authoritative: E = Hextech Ray 12/11/10/9/8s, W = Gravity Field 17-13s, R = Arcane Storm 120/100/80s flagged channel-interruptible.
audit.corrected: All name swaps applied across spikes, whys, early/mid/late, wants; cage-cancels-storm added; real cooldowns written into breakdown.cooldowns.

audit.why: Gravity Field 17s rank 1 / 13s max is the punish window; E 12-8s is his shove cadence.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d and dontsFull[2].d were verbatim tradeGood/tradeBad pasted under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED).
audit.why: Title promises one thing, body explains another.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to match their titles, grounded in Viktor's kit.

audit.whatIsWrong: Cage-cancels-Arcane-Storm channel interaction was absent everywhere.

edits.before: - Viktor Gravity Field: matchup-defining — The stun zone owns every all-in — walk out the moment it drops or fight outside it. Step up only on its downtime. - Budget E Event Horizon (self-cage) for emergencies and the R for opportunities — never swap them.
edits.after: - Gravity Field (W) is 17s at rank 1, 13s max — the stun zone owns every all-in, so step up only in that window. - His Arcane Storm (R, 120s) is a channel: your cage cancels it outright. - Your E is 20s early; once spent you have no anti-gank for 20 seconds.

edits.after: Cage where he must walk to farm; when he clips the edge, the stun buys a free W-Q before his 17s Gravity Field answers.

edits.before: W-ing open ground on a moving target and trading uncaged 'just to stack' — Veigar without the wall is a piggy bank with a hat.
edits.after: His Hextech Ray shoves for free on a 12s cooldown — matching every push walks you into poke; take what the wave gives and no more.

edits.before: Level 6 is roughly even — it's a skill check. Viktor's Chaos Storm (R) is a moving DPS/silence storm that pressures you at range, but a landed Event Horizon lets you W (Dark Matter) and R him before the storm wins the trade. Whoever lands their control tool first (your cage vs his W stun-field) takes the exchange, so it comes down to who commits cleaner.
edits.after: Level 6 is roughly even — it's a skill check. Viktor's Arcane Storm (R) is a moving damage storm, but it is a channel: your Event Horizon stun cancels the cast outright, and a landed cage lets you W (Dark Matter) and R him before the storm wins the trade. Whoever lands their control tool first (your cage vs his W stun-field) takes the exchange.

edits.before: Two-plus items is Veigar's: your Phenomenal Evil stacks give you literally uncapped AP, so your E-W-R deletes Viktor while his Chaos Storm needs time-on-target you deny by pillaring him in place. Land the cage in a teamfight and he simply dies; play the pick game and your infinite scaling out-damages his.
edits.after: Two-plus items is Veigar's: your Phenomenal Evil stacks give you literally uncapped AP, so your E-W-R deletes Viktor while his Arcane Storm needs time-on-target you deny by pinning him in place. This is a farm-and-scale phase where he's slightly ahead — just stay even on CS and healthy.

Play picks and your infinite scaling wins.
